design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (employer_instant_pay_disbursements, category disburse). Coordinator brief: env/env_0077 inst_common.txt read in full; identifier band phones 6465550100-199, tax 3xxx, surnames I-L, employer first word I-L.

[0 Draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 6]}. The root disburse_ext_early_closure_fee takes 6 factors, the prerequisite disburse_ext_closing_month_fee takes 4. Task 1 draw (for headroom): prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [5, 6, 4, 4].

[0 Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: the closure of the service (base disburse_lifecycle closure + the early-closure clause of disburse_evt_fees) and the platform fee of the month in which a service closes. Left for task 1: funding of a running service - the employer's own prefund deposit, the automatic replenishment debit, the alert level that drives it, and the platform fee of completed billing months (fee debit day). No task 1 asset can replace a task 0 one: task 1 never closes a service and never bills a closing month.

[0 Design thesis] Surface goal: the program owner asks to finish closing the Instant Pay service as requested in the portal. Core scored value: the early closure fee the employer confirms in person (28.41). Hidden prerequisite: the early-closure rule waits on the platform fee of the closing month being on the ledger, a fee the customer never mentions, which the agent must compute (7.90) and book first. Depth: 2 problems in a chain; breadth: 10 factors over the service ledger (fees, payouts, the closure request), the tier parameters, the employer's Earned Wage Access Program Agreement (program difficulty) and its Payroll Card Program (paycard difficulty). Negative space: the desk books no withdrawal of the remaining balance on the closing day (the closing run returns it on the next business day), although the customer asks about her money.

[0 Why a good test] A careless agent closes at once with the tier's flat early_closure_fee_usd (250.00, the fall-back of an agent who read only the computation document) or computes the fee before booking the closing-month platform fee (29.60). The right answer needs: discovering the prerequisite sentence, computing the closing-month fee from four rules (billed part by closing day, activity of the last month, EWA bundle, payroll-card migration), then six early-closure rules (starter-period measure against the platform fees actually debited since enrollment, notice relief from the closure request date, retention relief from the EWA agreement's renewal date against the service term, fee-model relief, volume relief from the payout count, setup relief from enrollment to activation), and handing the confirmation to the customer (owner=user: closing is the employer's own act; owner_ruling (a) - the employer's in-person confirmation together with the same-category consequence it books, the early closure fee).

[1 Policies] disburse_ext_closing_month_fee (on_request, subject disburse_fee, target book_closing_month_fee_4be79540, computes amount); base_policy_refs disburse_evt_fees, disburse_ewa_bundle (every base policy whose subject includes disburse_fee). Overwrites: (1) disburse_evt_fees fee-day clause, retired for the closing month only (replaced_by keeps the completed-month debit on the fee day); (2) disburse_ewa_bundle full-month clause, replaced for the closing month by a three-tier bundle ladder; (3) disburse_ewa_bundle 'holding a Payroll Card Program earns no discount here.', replaced for the closing month by the migration percentage, with a tail sending completed months to the completed-month rule. disburse_ext_early_closure_fee (on_request, subject disburse_close, target confirm_service_closure_f3d256bb owner=user, computes early_closure_fee); base_policy_refs disburse_lifecycle (subject disburse_close) and disburse_evt_fees (source of the early-closure clause it overwrites). Overwrites: (1) disburse_lifecycle 'A closure or recall is accepted only from a requester whose role is listed in authorized_requester_roles.' replaced by the narrower in-person confirmation of the contact who submitted the pending request (recall text restated); (2) disburse_evt_fees 'a closure before minimum_term_months from enrollment early_closure_fee_usd' replaced by the term sentence and the baseline sentence. Inherited and unchanged: 'A fee that comes to zero is not debited', 'Each fee points to the entry that incurred it' (platform and early-closure fees point to no ledger entry), 'Fees are debited from the prefund balance under the tier held on the day they are incurred', disburse_evt_prefund 'on closure the whole remaining balance is withdrawn to the employer's bank within remaining_balance_refund_business_days business days' (the next-business-day closing run is inside that window).

[1 Factor card - closing-month fee, 4 factors, 3 parameter + 1 method] cm_share (method; anchor family): activated during the closing month -> counted from activation date in thirds; activated earlier and closing on or before day 20 -> counted from the first of the month in thirds; otherwise whole month. World: activated 2026-09-17, closing 2026-11-17 (day 17) -> two thirds; baseline 1 -> 11.85. cm_activity (parameter): payouts in the month ending on the closing date (dates after 2026-10-17): 3 (2026-10-24 x2, 2026-10-31) -> light_use_multiplier 0.5; near-miss (round 3): two payouts sit on 2026-10-17, the excluded day-number boundary (exactly one whole month before the closing date): a reader who counts that day gets 5 payouts, no longer fewer than light_use_payouts, a multiplier of one and 15.80 instead of 7.90; baseline 1 -> 15.80. cm_bundle (parameter, cross-difficulty program): live agreement, go_live_date 2025-03-10 before the month -> 50 percent (Growth ewa_bundle_platform_fee_discount_percent); baseline 0 -> 21.07. cm_migration (parameter, cross-difficulty paycard): Payroll Card Program contracted, signed 2026-10-06, 1 whole month before closing -> 20 percent; baseline 0 -> 13.17. Assembly (generic sentence): 79.00 x 2/3 x 0.5 x (1 - 70/100) = 7.90; whole baseline 79.00.

[1 Factor card - early closure fee, 6 factors, 5 parameter + 1 method] etf_measure (method): <=3 months left -> list fee x months left; fewer than 3 whole months since enrollment and >3 left -> early_closure_fee_usd less platform fees debited since enrollment net of platform-fee credits, floor 0; otherwise flat. World: MONTHS(2026-09-02, 2026-11-17) = 2, 10 left -> 250.00 - (21.07 + 31.60 + 7.90) = 189.43; baseline flat 250 -> 37.50. etf_notice (parameter): request 2026-10-13, 35 days -> 20; near-miss (seeded): a duplicate closure request submitted 2026-10-28 and withdrawn is not the latest request still in submitted status - counting it gives 20 days, 10 percent and 47.36; baseline -> 66.30. etf_retention (parameter, multi-source over the agreement's status and renewal_date AND the service's enrolled_date/term, cross-difficulty program): live, renewal 2028-02-03 = 17 whole months after enrollment >= 12 -> 20; baseline -> 66.30. etf_fee_model (parameter, cross-difficulty program): employer_paid -> 15; baseline -> 56.83. etf_volume (parameter): 17 payouts in the 3-month window < 500 -> 20; baseline -> 66.30. etf_setup (parameter): 15 days enrollment->activation > 14 -> 10; baseline -> 47.36. Assembly: reliefs added into one rate (85) and applied once: 189.43 x 0.15 = 28.4145 -> 28.41; whole baseline 250.00. No stamp field names any tier; every tier rests on dates, counts, sums or the other products' records.

[1 Prerequisite card] Edge disburse_ext_early_closure_fee -> disburse_ext_closing_month_fee; kind value_input; gate platform_fees_paid; form state; policy_source 'For a service whose tier carries a monthly platform fee, the early closure fee is fixed only after the ledger carries the platform fee for the month in which the closure falls.' (round 2: the opening record test carves out tiers whose platform fee is zero, where no closing-month entry can exist) Four-point test: (1) ordering connective 'only after', affirmative direction, as a fee desk states a charge that rests on another charge; (2) waits on a record-visible state (a platform fee entry for the closing month on the ledger); (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) strength exact - the one entry of one billing month. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the closing-month fee booking (the completed-month platform fee of task 1 bills months that have ended, never the month of the closure). Derivation: sentence + ledger (fees only for 2026-09 and 2026-10) + the closing-month rule ('the platform fee is debited on the day the closure is taken ... booked as one platform fee entry for that billing month') -> book the closing-month fee first. Unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.disburse_ledger.<fee_sep>.billing_month = 2026-09, <fee_oct>.billing_month = 2026-10, no 2026-11 entry. Load: skipping it gives 29.60 instead of 28.41 and drops the 7.90 entry. Topological order: closing-month fee (step 8) then confirmation (step 10). user_scenario names no fee or charge; tools validate nothing (confirm_service_closure books whatever the ledger holds).

[1 Base-invariant card] Closing-month fee (subject disburse_fee): disburse_evt_fees.one_fee 'A source entry incurs at most one fee of each fee type, and the platform fee is debited once per billing month.' (dedup, system record): no monthly_platform entry exists for 2026-11 (ledger shows 2026-09 and 2026-10 only); correlation (related_entry_id empty, fee_type monthly_platform) bound to the latest platform fee row. disburse_ewa_bundle has no gate (policy_scope). Early closure (subject disburse_close): disburse_lifecycle.close_role is retired by the declared overwrite and replaced by the in-person confirmation of the contact who submitted the pending request; evidence disburse_requests.<rq>.requester_role = program_owner (listed in authorized_requester_roles), submitted by the caller (user_scenario 'the program owner'). The term test is a whole-month count from enrolled_date (not a time eligibility gate): MONTHS(2026-09-02, 2026-11-17) = 2 < 12 -> charged; a closure on 2027-09-02 (12 whole months) would be charged nothing, on 2027-09-01 it would still be inside the term. No temporal eligibility gate applies (temporal_feasibility []).

[1 Business-object card] Target object: service bd0d0b76-... (the employer's only disbursement service) and its pending closure request d99ef856-... (request_type service_closure, submitted, program_owner, 2026-10-13). Platform fees included in the starter-period measure: every disburse_fee with fee_type monthly_platform on the service (21.07 for 2026-09 debited 2026-10-05, 31.60 for 2026-10 debited 2026-11-04, the new 7.90 for 2026-11); excluded: deposits, payouts; no platform-fee credits exist. Payouts counted: 17 disburse_payout rows (2026-09-19..2026-10-31), 3 of them in the closing-month activity window (2026-10-24 x2, 2026-10-31); the two 2026-10-17 payouts sit on the excluded boundary day.

[3 Seed] Employer Kittredge Hall Events LLC (customers, phone 6465550142, EIN last4 3418, ZIP 60607). Service: Paystride Instant Pay Growth, enrolled 2026-09-02, activated 2026-09-17, employer_ach_credit, auto_replenish false, alert 500.00 (Growth default), balance 2359.03 = 7500.00 deposits - 5088.30 payouts - 52.67 fees. Deposits 2026-09-04 5000.00 and 2026-10-07 2500.00 (ACH credits, available after 1 business day). 17 payouts to four payees (employee numbers 3104, 3117, 3122, 3139) by external debit card (delivered in 2-6 minutes, inside the 30-minute SLA -> no late-delivery credit owed) or bank account; all within the 500 included disbursements -> no per-disbursement fee owed; no Paystride card destination -> no card load trigger. Platform fees priced by the completed-month rule as of their posting: 2026-09 = 79.00 x 2/3 (activated day 17) x (1 - (50 EWA bundle + 10 employer_paid fee model)/100) = 21.07; 2026-10 = 79.00 x (1 - 60/100) = 31.60; no program-size percentage (Paystride Program Growth); a Payroll Card Program earns no discount on a completed month. Volume review: complete months since activation are 2026-09 and 2026-10 only (< volume_review_consecutive_months 3) -> no tier move owed. Cross-difficulty rows: program_agreements (Paystride Program Growth for 228 eligible employees (band 50-249), live since 2025-03-10, signed 2025-02-03, term 36, renewal 2028-02-03 = signed + term, employer_paid, receivables 0.00, so nothing is owed on that product) and paycard_programs (Standard, contracted, signed 2026-10-06, not launched, zero balance and kits - the state paycard_agg_multi_holding opens a program in; no ledger exists before launch). Payee worker profiles are not seeded: no decision reads them and the replay closure excludes them; payouts carry their ids and employee numbers. Automatic clauses checked: auto replenishment off; returned deposits none; courtesy credits none; fee debit days 2026-10-05 and 2026-11-04 already booked; nothing else falls due by 2026-11-17.

[4 Persona] Danielle Laurent (surname L), program owner, brisk and organized. Volunteers only the goal (finish closing the service as asked in the portal) and the reason (tips move to payroll). Gives name, phone and email for verification, ZIP/EIN only if a third detail is asked; other Paystride programs only if asked (cross-category holdings are not volunteered). Passive: agrees when told a charge must be booked first; asks once whether she must do anything to get the remaining money back (answered by the rule with no write: the closing run returns it the next business day); runs the confirmation herself with the exact figures; ends when the closure is confirmed. No line names the closing-month fee, the platform fee or any prerequisite.

[5 Verification] verify.py (scratch, replays the real tools) output: step 0 closing-month fee expected 7.9; cm_share 11.85, cm_activity 15.8, cm_bundle 21.07, cm_migration 13.17, ALL-BASELINE 79.0; step 1 early closure fee expected 28.41; etf_measure 37.5, etf_notice 66.3, etf_retention 66.3, etf_fee_model 56.83, etf_volume 66.3, etf_setup 47.36, ALL-BASELINE 250.0; SKIP step 0 -> early closure fee 29.6. Gates (--task 0): check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK (closure 25 = init 25); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK; check_traceability (pre-docs) misses only the two unlock tool names, as expected before rendering. Revision log: (r1) check_task_tools FAIL 'must still state precision' -> wrote '2 decimal places'; (r2) check_solvability needs the one_fee dedup arguments -> the closing-month tool now takes fee_type (monthly_platform only) and related_entry_id (empty only), the tool refusing anything else; the close_role gate (mixed authority over a one-field correlation key) is retired by a real narrowing overwrite; the early closure policy's subject is the closure; (r3) check_compute 'history is NOT load-bearing' (the activity factor read only LATEST) -> activity now counts payouts in the month ending on the closing date; (r4) replay closure mismatch (4 payee profiles unread) -> profiles dropped; (r5) sweep found the early-closure result basis non-contiguous and two params unnamed in the rule -> basis = assembly sentence, params removed (thirds and the one-month window written into the sentences and the compute).

[XF recipe sweep] A1 factor-reads table (transitive): cm_share <- activated_date, NOW, month_index(plain); cm_activity <- COUNT payouts; cm_bundle <- CFIELD program go_live_date, month_index(plain); cm_migration <- CFIELD paycard signed_date, EXISTS paycard live; etf_measure <- months_since_enrollment(plain), SUM platform fees/credits, tier params; etf_notice <- LATEST closure request; etf_retention <- CFIELD program renewal_date, enrolled_date; etf_fee_model <- CFIELD program fee_model; etf_volume <- COUNT payouts, tier allowance; etf_setup <- enrolled_date, activated_date. No factor reads another factor's binding. A2/A3: assembly sentences are generic ('every multiplier that applies below ... the percentages being added together into one rate rather than applied one after another'); multipliers commute, percentages are summed, rounding once. A4 defining-sentence table: month_index (share_b sentence) used by cm_share and cm_bundle -> plain; months_since_enrollment (term sentence) used by the term test and etf_measure -> plain; platform_fees_paid (measure_b sentence) used only by etf_measure -> its binding. A6 all-pairs method tiers: cm_share (a) DAYS(activation, closing) thirds vs (b) day-of-month thresholds vs (c) constant 1 - each pair differs by an input; etf_measure (a) list fee x months left vs (b) flat - SUM(platform fees) with floor vs (c) flat - each pair differs by an input/operation. A7: MX(0, flat - fees) floor never binds on this world (fees 60.57 < 250); T1 holds for every factor (each sensitivity differs); T2: each factor moves the result with the others at baseline (e.g. etf_notice alone: 250 x 0.8 = 200.00). A8: no factor id is a substring of a tool name (sweep.py). B1/B2 probe table (probe_t0.py, scratch copies): no payouts ever -> activity 0.25 (3.95); payout return in November -> ignored (7.90); terminated older agreement listed first -> ignored (status filter); no agreement -> bundle 0 (21.07), retention 0, fee model 0 (ETF 98.67 at opening); terminated paycard listed first -> ignored; paycard live -> 10 percent (10.53); contracted paycard signed exactly 3 months before -> 0 (13.17); no paycard -> 0; later withdrawn closure request -> ignored (status filter); no closure request -> notice 0 (ETF 69.07 at opening); request 29 days before -> 10 (49.33). Ties: two submitted closure requests on one day give the same submitted_date. B4: compute RND(x+1e-9,2), tools Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP; all figures > 1e-6 from a half cent (7.8999, 28.4145, 11.85, 15.80, 21.0667, 13.1667, 37.50, 66.3005, 56.829, 47.3575, 29.5995). B5: sweep.py - every compute_basis quote, baseline sentence, replaced_by and prerequisite sentence is verbatim in its rule. Events written with base triggers: disburse_fee (triggers []), disburse_close (triggers []); no payout is written. E2: the reads of the other products (agreement status/go_live_date/renewal_date/fee_model, paycard status/signed_date) cannot be moved by anything owed at once on those products at 2026-11-17.

[6 Standard solution] find_customers(name) -> verify (phone, email) -> find_disburse_services -> find_disburse_requests -> find_disburse_ledger -> find_program_agreements -> find_paycard_programs -> unlock + call book_closing_month_fee (service, monthly_platform, '', 7.90) -> unlock_user + hand over confirm_service_closure (service, request, 28.41), run by the customer. Terminal state: 2026-11 platform fee 7.90 and early closure fee 28.41 on the ledger, service closed 2026-11-17, request confirmed, balance 2322.70 (returned by the closing run next business day; no withdrawal booked).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Using only the rules as they will be published, the tool schemas, the persona lines and the finder returns: the closure request and term sentence say the fee is owed (2 whole months into a 12-month term); the prerequisite sentence and the ledger (no 2026-11 platform fee) say book the closing-month fee first; its four rules give 79 x 2/3 x 0.5 x 0.3 = 7.90; the early-closure rules then give 189.43 x 0.15 = 28.41; the confirmation is the customer's own act. Same objects, order and figures as gold; no second reading found.


[REWORK round 2] Audit items closed (audits/policy_task/employer_instant_pay_disbursements, revision_1): F-1 - the closing-month rule no longer states the order of the closure confirmation ('is debited on the day the closure is taken and is worked out as set out here'); the dependency lives only in the early-closure prerequisite sentence; the step-8 action_semantics now cites that sentence. F-2 - the prerequisite sentence opens with the record test 'For a service whose tier carries a monthly platform fee', so a tier with a zero platform fee (no closing-month entry can exist) is outside the wait; the edge condition says the same; on every tier with a fee the closing-month fee is above zero (smallest third, quarter activity and 70 percent reductions still leave 29.00 x 1/3 x 0.25 x 0.3 = 0.725), so the resolver always books an entry. F-5 - 'whole months left' is defined as minimum_term_months less the whole months from the enrolled_date to the closing date (the compute's months_left_in_term). F-6 - every whole-month count states the convention 'the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's' (term, retention, migration), every month window states 'every payout dated fewer than N whole months before the closing date' (activity, volume), and every day count states which end is counted (billed part from activation, notice, setup). T0-F1 - seeded near-miss: a duplicate service-closure request submitted 2026-10-28 and withdrawn; a reader who takes the latest request whatever its status gets 20 days, 10 percent notice relief and 47.36 instead of 28.41. O-7 - the closing-month bundle overwrite tail now repeats the half-up rounding. Realism note on the tier (audit observation): the service opened at Growth on the employer's expected volume (an events business with 228 eligible staff working about a dozen events a month), and the actual volume never reached the band - which is what the volume relief prices. Re-run after the changes: verify.py gives the same figures (closing-month fee 7.90, early closure fee 28.41, skip -> 29.60; sensitivities unchanged); probes unchanged plus the withdrawn-request probe above.

[REWORK round 3] T0-F1 residual (closing-month computation had no discriminating near-miss) closed in the seed only: a second tips payout dated 2026-10-17 (payee 3117, external debit card, 3 minutes) now sits with the existing 2026-10-17 payout on the window's excluded boundary day - exactly one whole month before the closing date. The rule ('every payout dated fewer than one whole month before the closing date') excludes both, leaving 3 payouts and the light-use multiplier; a reader who counts the boundary day gets 5 payouts, which is not fewer than light_use_payouts, a multiplier of one and 15.80 instead of 7.90. Nothing else moves: the payout is inside the 500 included disbursements (no per-disbursement fee), delivered inside the SLA, funded from available money, inside the early-closure volume window (17 payouts, still below the allowance, same relief), and the platform fees and closure request are untouched; balance 2359.03, terminal balance 2322.70. Charter and tools unchanged; task 1 unchanged. verify.py: closing-month fee 7.90, early closure fee 28.41, skip -> 29.60, every sensitivity unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Danielle Laurent, the owner and Paystride program owner of Kittredge Hall Events LLC, an event venue and catering company in Chicago. It is a Tuesday morning and you are calling Paystride's employer support desk from your office, organized and a little brisk, with your own notes open in front of you. Last month, on October 13, you sent a request through the employer portal to close the company's Instant Pay Disbursement service as of today, because from now on your event staff's tips and extra pay will go through regular payroll. You open the call by saying that you'd like to finish closing Kittredge Hall's Instant Pay service today, as you asked in the portal last month. You understand that closing the service is something you confirm yourself, and you are ready to do that on this call.

When the agent asks who you are, you give the business name, Kittredge Hall Events LLC, and say you are Danielle Laurent, the program owner. For verification you give the phone number on the account, 6465550142, and your work email, dlaurent@kittredgehallevents.com; if a third detail is wanted you can give the billing ZIP code, 60607, or the last four digits of the company's EIN, 3418. You do not keep any Paystride reference numbers and leave every lookup to the agent. Only if the agent asks whether the company uses other Paystride programs do you say that Kittredge Hall runs Paystride Earned Wage Access for its staff and signed up for a Paystride Payroll Card Program in October that hasn't started yet; you don't know their details beyond that.

You have no idea what closing will cost and you never suggest a figure. If the agent explains that a charge has to be put on the account before the closure can go through, you say that's fine and to go ahead. Before you confirm anything, you ask once whether you need to do anything yourself to get the money left in the account back, and you accept whatever the agent tells you. When the agent tells you the early closure fee and hands the closure confirmation over to you, you run it yourself straight away with exactly the service reference, the closure request reference and the fee amount the agent gives you, without changing anything; if the agent asks you to confirm without telling you the fee, you first ask what the fee will be. Once the confirmation comes back showing the service closed, you thank the agent and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the employer profile of Kittredge Hall Events LLC by the business name the caller states.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write is keyed on the employer's customer reference; the caller knows only the business name.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the caller is the employer on file with two matching credentials (phone and email).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be confirmed before any account detail is discussed or any money is moved.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Instant Pay Disbursement service: tier Paystride Instant Pay Growth, status active, enrolled_date 2026-09-02, activated_date 2026-09-17, prefund_balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier fixes monthly_platform_fee_usd, early_closure_fee_usd, minimum_term_months and included_disbursements_per_month; enrolled_date and activated_date drive the term, setup and billed-part tests.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the service-closure requests: the pending one (requester_role program_owner, request_status submitted, submitted_date 2026-10-13) and a duplicate submitted 2026-10-28 and withdrawn.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The pending request's reference is the object the employer confirms, its submitted_date decides the notice relief (the withdrawn duplicate does not count), and its role is the authorized-contact check.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole service ledger: the platform fees debited for 2026-09 and 2026-10 (none for 2026-11), the payouts with their dates and the deposits.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that no platform fee stands for the closing month (the state the early closure fee waits on), gives the latest payout date for the activity multiplier, the platform fees debited since enrollment and the payout count of the volume window.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's Earned Wage Access Program Agreement: status live, go_live_date 2025-03-10, renewal_date 2028-02-03, fee_model employer_paid.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Decides the closing-month bundle percentage (go-live before the month), the retention relief (renewal_date against the service's term) and the fee-model relief.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's Payroll Card Program: status contracted, signed_date 2026-10-06, not launched.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Decides the closing-month migration percentage (contracted program signed fewer than three whole months before the closing date).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the closing-month platform fee booking.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Debit the November 2026 platform fee of the closing month (7.90 USD) so the ledger carries the platform fee for the month in which the closure falls.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: disburse_ext_closing_month_fee computes the amount; disburse_ext_early_closure_fee is fixed only after this entry exists.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 7.90 = RND(monthly_platform_fee_usd 79.00 x billed part 2/3 (cm_share: activated 2026-09-17 in an earlier month, closing on day 17) x activity multiplier 0.5 (cm_activity: 3 payouts dated after 2026-10-17, fewer than 5) x (1 - (bundle 50 [cm_bundle: live agreement, go-live 2025-03-10] + migration 20 [cm_migration: paycard contracted, signed 2026-10-06]) / 100) + 1e-9, 2), evaluated on the opening world (this is the first write). Any agent applying the closing-month rule to these records reaches 7.90; the computation document alone gives 79.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.disburse_service_id: bd0d0b76-6fbf-49ef-9c03-a732809e7c02; basis: the tool docstring 'the reference number of the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service, read from the service record returned by the service lookup' and the find_disburse_services return for the verified employer; uniqueness: the employer holds exactly one disbursement service (disburse_agg_multi_holding: 'An employer may not hold a second disbursement service that is not closed.').
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_type: monthly_platform; basis: the docstring 'monthly_platform — the platform fee of the month in which the service is closing, the only kind of fee this tool books' and the closing-month rule 'booked as one platform fee entry for that billing month'; uniqueness: the enum has this single value and every other fee kind books nothing.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_entry_id: '' (empty); basis: the docstring 'a closing-month platform fee arises from no ledger entry, so it is passed as an empty string' and the rule 'booked as one platform fee entry for that billing month that points to no source entry'; uniqueness: any non-empty value books nothing.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the employer's own closure confirmation so it can be handed to the program owner.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own write; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The program owner confirms the closure in person: the service closes on 2026-11-17, the request is confirmed and the 28.41 USD early closure fee is debited.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: disburse_ext_early_closure_fee computes early_closure_fee; closing the service is the employer's own act.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.early_closure_fee: 28.41 = RND(MX(0, measured 189.43 x (1 - 85/100)) + 1e-9, 2), evaluated after step 8 landed: measured = early_closure_fee_usd 250.00 - platform fees debited since enrollment (21.07 + 31.60 + 7.90 from step 8) under the starter-period measure (etf_measure: 2 whole months since 2026-09-02, 10 left); reliefs notice 20 (request 2026-10-13, 35 days) + retention 20 (live agreement renewing 2028-02-03, 17 months after enrollment) + fee model 15 (employer_paid) + volume 20 (17 payouts < 500) + setup 10 (activated 15 days after enrollment). Without step 8 the same reading gives 29.60; the computation document alone gives 250.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.disburse_service_id: bd0d0b76-6fbf-49ef-9c03-a732809e7c02; basis: the docstring 'the reference number of the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service, as read to the employer by the desk from the service record' and the find_disburse_services return; uniqueness: the employer's only disbursement service.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.disburse_request_id: d99ef856-d3ca-4ec3-a538-7af88531f583; basis: the docstring 'the reference number of the employer's pending service-closure request, as read to the employer by the desk from the request record' and the find_disburse_requests return (request_type service_closure, request_status submitted, requester_role program_owner); uniqueness: it is the only service-closure request still in submitted status (the 2026-10-28 duplicate is withdrawn) and the one the program owner submitted on 2026-10-13.

factor_trace: cm_share (method): service activated 2026-09-17 (an earlier month) and the closure is on 2026-11-17, day 17 of the closing month (on or before day second_third_days=20, after day first_third_days=10) -> billed part counted from the first day of the month = two thirds; the baseline bills the whole month (multiplier 1), giving 11.85.

cm_activity (parameter): payouts dated after 2026-10-17 (activity_window_months 1): 2026-10-24 (two) and 2026-10-31 (one) = 3, at least one but fewer than light_use_payouts 5 -> light_use_multiplier 0.5 (near-miss: two payouts sit on 2026-10-17, the excluded day-number boundary (exactly one whole month before the closing date): a reader who counts that day gets 5 payouts, no longer fewer than light_use_payouts, a multiplier of one and 15.80 instead of 7.90; the 12 earlier payouts are plainly outside the month); baseline multiplier 1 gives 15.80.

cm_bundle (parameter, cross-difficulty program): program_agreements.375fa562-1224-4a63-932e-b5e7f0ef84ca status live, go_live_date 2025-03-10 (before the first day of 2026-11) -> P('ewa_bundle_platform_fee_discount_percent') = 50 for Paystride Instant Pay Growth; baseline 0 percent gives 21.07.

cm_migration (parameter, cross-difficulty paycard): paycard_programs.dfa39930-154c-495f-8596-195b3ff583de status contracted, signed_date 2026-10-06, MONTHS(2026-10-06, 2026-11-17) = 1 < migration_window_months 3 -> migration_contracted_percent 20; baseline 0 percent gives 13.17.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the service was activated in an earlier month and the closure falls on or before day second_third_days of the closing month
at least one but fewer than light_use_payouts payouts were sent in that month
the employer's Earned Wage Access Program Agreement is live and went live on or before the first day of the closing month
the employer's Payroll Card Program is in contracted status and was signed fewer than migration_window_months whole months before the closing date

factor_trace: etf_measure (method): months since enrollment MONTHS(2026-09-02, 2026-11-17) = 2 < starter_period_months 3, months left 12 - 2 = 10 > end_of_term_months 3 -> starter-period measure = early_closure_fee_usd 250.00 less the platform fees debited since enrollment at handling time (disburse_ledger.be37399a-6af3-401f-a26d-4a9ebc97ea8a 21.07 + disburse_ledger.6636763d-1f7a-485f-982b-a7f157fae828 31.60 + the closing-month fee 7.90 booked at step 8 = 60.57; no platform fee credits) = 189.43; the baseline flat fee 250.00 gives 37.50.

etf_notice (parameter): disburse_requests.d99ef856-d3ca-4ec3-a538-7af88531f583 service_closure, status submitted, submitted_date 2026-10-13; DAYS(2026-10-13, 2026-11-17) = 35 >= notice_long_days 30 -> notice_long_percent 20; near-miss: the duplicate request submitted 2026-10-28 is withdrawn and is not the latest request still in submitted status (counting it would give 20 days -> 10 percent and 47.36); baseline 0 gives 66.30.

etf_retention (parameter, cross-difficulty program, multi-source): agreement 375fa562-1224-4a63-932e-b5e7f0ef84ca is live AND renewal_date 2028-02-03 is MONTHS(2026-09-02, 2028-02-03) = 17 >= minimum_term_months 12 whole months after the service's enrolled_date -> retention_long_percent 20; baseline 0 gives 66.30.
etf_fee_model (parameter, cross-difficulty program): live agreement fee_model employer_paid -> fee_model_paid_percent 15; baseline 0 gives 56.83.
etf_volume (parameter): 17 payouts dated after 2026-08-17 (volume_window_months 3) < included_disbursements_per_month 500 -> volume_low_percent 20; baseline 0 gives 66.30.
etf_setup (parameter): DAYS(2026-09-02, 2026-09-17) = 15 > setup_long_days 14 -> setup_long_percent 10; baseline 0 gives 47.36.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: fewer than starter_period_months whole months have passed since enrollment and more than end_of_term_months are left
the latest submitted service-closure request was submitted at least notice_long_days days before the closing date
the employer's Earned Wage Access Program Agreement is live and its renewal_date is at least minimum_term_months whole months after the service's enrolled_date
the employer's live agreement is on the employer_paid fee model
fewer payouts were booked in the window than one month's included_disbursements_per_month
the service was activated more than setup_long_days days after its enrolled_date

edges.condition: disburse_ledger holds, for the service, a disburse_fee entry with fee_type monthly_platform whose billing_month is the month of the closing date
edges.policy_source: For a service whose tier carries a monthly platform fee, the early closure fee is fixed only after the ledger carries the platform fee for the month in which the closure falls.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-11-17 the service's platform fee entries are for billing months 2026-09 and 2026-10 only; no platform fee entry for 2026-11, the month of the closure, exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 8 books a disburse_fee entry with fee_type monthly_platform, billing_month 2026-11, amount 7.90; platform_fees_paid rises from 52.67 to 60.57 and the measured early closure fee falls from 197.33 to 189.43.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite edge: the closing-month platform fee must be written before the early closure fee, as the prerequisite sentence 'The early closure fee is fixed only after the ledger carries the platform fee for the month in which the closure falls.' states; there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder. The reverse order is wrong: the early closure fee computed first reads platform fees of 52.67 and gives 29.60, not 28.41.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 8 (verify.py SKIP run) leaves platform_fees_paid at 52.67, so early_closure_fee becomes 29.60 instead of 28.41, and the 2026-11 platform fee entry (7.90) is missing from the terminal ledger.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to finish closing the Instant Pay service; it never mentions a platform fee, the closing month's billing or any charge to be booked first. The only related line is passive: 'If the agent explains that a charge has to be put on the account before the closure can go through, you say that's fine and to go ahead.', which fires only after the agent raises it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_service_closure_f3d256bb (task_tools.py) updates the service to closed, the request to confirmed and books the fee whatever the ledger holds; it never reads the platform fee entries and returns no error when the closing-month fee is missing. book_closing_month_fee_4be79540 likewise books whenever its fee kind and source arguments are well-formed.
